gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-pridi: Pridi has small letters that stand almost as tall as capitals. Edo SZ answers with cast-iron lowercase and one constant stroke, while Pridi offers generous curves that open gently toward the stem.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-slabo-13px: Edo SZ stamps its lowercase out like a stencil-cut channel, every stroke the same width. Slabo 13px follows in a text serif that feels dignified and bookish.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-suwannaphum: Lowercase letters with the stature of cast-iron capitals mark Edo SZ, all drawn in a single constant stroke. Suwannaphum is the classic serif counterpart, with a high x-height like squared woodblock type.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-inter: Cast-iron lowercase built from one constant stroke gives Edo SZ its weight. Inter sits beneath in a sans with big counters and a smooth, tube-like line, so the heavy heading and the hollow-reed text each get their own space.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-mulish: Mulish reads modern and friendly, with no thick-and-thin shifts anywhere. Its large x-height and horseshoe-open apertures keep a full page moving smoothly under Edo SZ, whose cast-iron lowercase holds the top.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-bitter: Eight Bit Dragon strides across widely spaced, towering lowercase letters with a small, steady shift in stroke thickness. Bitter grounds it as a slab-serif with a very large lowercase eye and an s you can see straight through.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-epunda-sl: Widely separated letters and a towering lowercase give Eight Bit Dragon a relaxed stride. And Epunda Slab brings tall rounded forms with a visibly gaping c, which is the serif's real strength.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-fauna-one: Fauna One has a tall middle band with shallow ascenders and descenders. Paragraphs in it feel literary and dignified, with each e inviting you in, while Eight Bit Dragon sits above with its modest thick-and-thin rhythm.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-hanuman: Hanuman is a traditional, refined serif with a high-waisted lowercase and wide-set terminals on the s. Hanuman needs a little more size than the towering Eight Bit Dragon heading to hold its own, so a slight bump is worth trying.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-kadwa: Wide-striding, tall, and a bit rebellious. Eight Bit Dragon is best at bold headings with lighter horizontals, and Kadwa is best at text serif paragraphs with open-ended curves and a larger-than-usual x-height.
